page: Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M processor configured with 2 physical cores and 4 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Hardware instruction support includes AVX-512, AVX, AES-NI, and FMA. Memory capacity is set at 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and features no dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the c5.xlarge primarily in the lower quartiles among modern cloud instances due to its older Skylake-era architecture and low core count. Single-threaded operations perform moderately, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1493.19 and a Clang compilation score of 3457.0. However, multi-core capacity is limited, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core rating of 2536.0 and PassMark CPU score of 4592.75. Memory performance remains restrained, recording large-block uncached read speeds of 26.42 GB/s and a write throughput of 23.29 GB/s.

From a cost-efficiency standpoint, the absence of local NVMe storage requires external Elastic Block Store volumes for persistent data, which increases total deployment footprint. The instance is suited for moderate compute-focused batch tasks, small web services, CI/CD worker nodes, and basic microservice hosting where high memory capacity and extreme parallel throughput are not required.
description: Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and a 3.4 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8124M CPU. It features 2 physical cores, 4 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. Designed without local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, the instance relies on remote block storage and features a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. In benchmark assessments, it demonstrates mid-tier single-threaded capability alongside lower multi-core output, reflecting its modest 4-thread count. Cache sizes include a 24 MB L3 allocation, and CPU instruction support spans AVX-512 and AES-NI. Given its compute-to-RAM balance and lack of bundled local disks, the c5.xlarge serves workloads such as lightweight application servers, continuous integration build jobs, distributed microservices, and general compute batch processing.
